key_insight: A GPT2 table-to-text approach can outperform traditional ML and neural networks for disease prediction on small, imbalanced clinical datasets by leveraging contextual clinical reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a potentially useful, interpretable way to improve prediction from low-volume structured health records where standard models may miss clinically meaningful patterns.
method: Converted structured clinical variables into physician-style text
Used GPT4 paraphrasing to augment minority-class examples
Fine-tuned GPT2 and added gradient-based explainability across four public datasets
evidence_signal: Across heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and thyroid cancer recurrence datasets, the model reported average precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.96, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.96, respectively.
watch_item: Because the approach relies on synthetic paraphrasing and public low-volume datasets, real-world validation is needed to confirm robustness, generalizability, and safety before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
